chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, and from Hammad, from al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who hastens during the two days, so he should not depart until the sun declines. So if evening overtakes him, he should spend the night and not depart.

key_terms.يَوْمَيْنِ: The two days (referring to the 11th and 12th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for leaving Mina early during Hajj if one does not stay until sunset?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal status of early departure (ta'ajjul) from Mina, establishing that leaving before solar noon invalidates the 'early' status, effectively treating the pilgrim as if they stayed the full day. It underscores the scholarly emphasis on balancing convenience with the ritual integrity of the Hajj days, ensuring that early departers do not rush off before the prescribed time for departure has fully commenced.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, and from Hammad, from al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who hastens during the two days, so he should not depart until the sun (starts to) decline. So if he sees the evening, he should spend the night and not depart’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar and Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Whoever departs earlier in the second day he cannot do so before Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime), and if it becomes evening he must stay for the night, instead of departing.”
